At the very outset, learned counsel for the revisionists submits that the revisionist no.3 namely Fattey Bind and in this regard, the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ghazipur has submitted its rep[ort dated 12.06.2017, which is on record.
Accordingly, the instant revision as against the revisionist no.3 Fattey Bind is dismissed as abated.

Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and the learned A.G.A.
Present criminal revision has been filed against the judgment and order of conviction dated 17.07.2002 passed by learnedAdditional Sessions Judge (N.D.P.S. Act) Court No. First, District Ghazipur in Criminal Appeal No. 24 of 1999 whereby order of IVth Additional Civil Judge (Junior Division)/ Magistrfate Ghazipur dated 11.03.1999 passed in Case No. 835 of 1998 (State Vs. Kishore Bind) has been affirmed and the revisionist has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment of one Alakh Niranjan Pal vs State Of U.P. And Others on 1 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130311325/
1 month along with fine of Rs. 200/- and awarding fine of Rs. 200/- for the offence under Section 504 I.P.C. and in case of default of payment of fine to further undergo imprisonment of ten days.
Learned counsel for the revisionist contends that from the date of order of the learned Magistrate,
more than 23 years have elapsed and the revisionist is an old ailing person and therefore, sentence of punishment may be converted into fine.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the revisionist has relied upon the judgment of this Court reported in 2004 (49) ACC 539 in the matter of Majister @ Budhpal versus State of U.P. wherein this Court has taken note of the fact that 19 years have elapsed since the date of revision and the accused was on bail during the pendency of revision and therefore, sending the accused to jail after lapse of 17 years would be against humanitarian approach and therefore, liberty was given to avail the benefit of provisions of Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. and the imprisonment was converted into fine.

sentences.text:
Paragraph 8, relevant part of paragraph-9 and paragraph 10 of the aforesaid judgment is quoted hereinunder:-
"8. Section 433 (d) aforesaid provides for commutation of sentence of simple imprisonment for fine by the appropriate Government.

In the leading case of N.
Sukumaran Nair v. Food Inspector, Mavelikara

entities.text:
N.
Sukumaran Nair v. Food Inspector, Mavelikara
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Supreme Court in such circumstances provided such relief as being permissible to an accused.
Para 3 of the judgment is extracted below-
"The offence took place in the year 1984.
The appellant has been awarded six months simple imprisonment and has also been ordered to pay a fine of Rs. 1000.
Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the Trial Court a sum of Rs. 6,000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.
On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalize the matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure."

9. In the case of Maqbool Ahamed v. State of U.P.(supra), learned Single Judge of this Court relying upon the aforesaid N. Sukumaran Nair v. Food Inspector, Mavelikara, altered the sentence awarded in such a case of food adulteration to the accused to six months simple imprisonment and also directed the State Government that instead of sentence of actual imprisonment he would pay fine which shall be deposited within stipulated period and then he would move an application before the State Government which on receipt of such application shall formalize the matter under the provisions of section 433 (d) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel for the revisionist, learned A.G.A. and after perusing the judgment and order impugned as well as the averments contained in the present revision, this Court is of the opinion that as 20 years have elapsed since the date of revision and the revisionist has remained on bail during the pendency of revision, this Court thinks appropriate for commutation of sentence whereby more than two decades have gone by.

This Court, therefore, directs the revisionist to deposit before the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Ghazipur a sum of Rs. 500/- as fine in commutation of sentence of his setence within a period of two months from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.
On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalize the matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
With the aforesaid directions, present revision is finally disposed of.
